semantic_nodes.canonical_text: 2.3 Safety information on patient transport and positioning
For safe and secure patient transport and patient positioning, observe the following sections depending on your workflow.
WARNING
Incorrect patient positioning, unintended patient movement, and unobserved movement of the patient table or gantry!
Injury to the patient, for example, contusions of the patient's extremities and unusable radiation.
◆ Always fix the patient with accessories, as described in the instructions for use, to avoid unintentional patient movement. For example, use restraint straps and arm supports.

◆ Monitor the patient continuously as long as the table top and gantry are moving. Take special care if the tilt of the gantry is anything other than zero degrees or the table height is anything other than the isocenter.

◆ Make sure that nothing can get caught while the table or gantry are moving. For example, parts of the body or clothing, any needles, infusion tubes, respiration tubes, catheters, ECG cables, or sheets and blankets.
◆ Follow the markings and labels on the equipment.
◆ Press a STOP key if an injury to the patient can occur.
WARNING
Incorrect patient positioning!
Injury to the patient or personnel, and damage to the equipment.
◆ Always verify that the patient is correctly positioned.
◆ Always observe the patient during system movements.

2 Safety information
WARNING
Incorrect patient positioning!
Injury to the patient by moving parts.
◆ Make sure that neither the patient's clothing nor hair can get caught in mechanical parts.

◆ Make sure that infusion lines and respiration tubes, catheters and ECG cables cannot get caught in the space between the table top and the side parts. These components must not be put under tensile stress in any other way.
◆ Make sure that patient bedding cannot get caught by moving parts of the patient table.
◆ Use positioning aids as described.
The patient table and accessories are designed for certain maximum loads.
WARNING
Exceeding the maximum load of the equipment, for example, patient table, overlays, accessories, and the assembly of accessories!
Injury to the patient or the personnel, or damage to the equipment.
◆ Make sure that the permissible maximum load of the equipment is not exceeded. The permissible maximum load of the equipment is displayed on the applied labels.
◆ Verify that the permissible maximum load is not exceeded for:
Each single item of equipment applied or plugged into the patient table. For example, positioning aids and overlays.
Equipment to which other equipment is attached. For example, accessory rail or infusion bottle holder.
The patient must always be positioned on the patient table.
Never position the patient directly in the gantry!

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: 9.3.9 Performing Image Inspection
The function Image inspection is available only for IEC standard 61223-3-5 (Ed. 2).
During the homogeneity test and the pixel noise test water images are generated. You need to inspect those images at the end of the constancy test and exclude any artifacts in the results.
You have performed the homogeneity test. ( Page 445 Performing the homogeneity test)
You have performed the pixel noise test. ( Page 445 Performing the pixel noise test)

9 Quality assurance
You have selected the required images in the Patient Browser .
◆ A list of noise and homogeneity images is displayed in the Viewing task card. Check the items in the Viewing task card. If there are no artifacts, confirm.
Confirmed images are removed from the list.
A report is generated that contains the study and series names of the inspected images.
